Last year in May, I visited New York City for the first time, and Times Square in Manhattan was absolutely one of the most iconic places I could not miss—and one I will never forget. …

NYC’s Times Square in winter is simply magical!
• I was able to pass by Times Square almost every day during my stay in Manhattan. It was walkable from my hotel. …

The fabulously famous Times Square!!

Hotel was literally a 5 minute walk… I had never been here and always wanted to …

This had to be on the tick list as I have been meaning to just walk down here and take some photos, but even though it has been over a foot of snow the night before and it was freezing, it was sort of better in a way as it wasn't as busy! …

What's not to love about one of the most iconic spots in America.  The world is a better place because of Times Square and there is a lot to see and do here like seeing the red steps, watch a live performance on the streets, watch a …

The beating heart of the city that never sleeps!
Times Square is an absolute sensory overload in the best way possible. It’s where NYC’s rich history meets modern-day spectacle. Whether you’re there at 10 AM …

My favorite place in the world is New York in the United States, because it's a beautiful city. There are interesting places to visit. You can walk in Central Park and visit Times Square and take pictures at Summit One Vanderbilt. The best time to visit is in December because Christmas is beautiful. You can enjoy the snow.

Stopped by Joe’s Pizza while in NYC. It’s solid for one thing: cheap, classic New York slices. If you want a quick, no-frills cheese slice that won’t destroy your wallet, this is your spot. It’s fast, straightforward, and exactly what you’d expect from a busy counter service pizza place. Nothing fancy, no crazy toppings just a simple slice you can fold and eat on the go. That said, I wouldn’t call it life changing. It’s good for what it is: affordable pizza in a prime location. If you’re expecting some mind blowing culinary experience, this isn’t that. But if you just want a cheap slice that gets the job done, Joe’s works.

Cash only, $5.50 for pepperoni slice and $4.50 for regular. Customer service is apathetic, no greetings. I did take out and they barely had the pizza in the oven for a minute before handing it to me. No napkins. The pizza is ok, not a bad pizza, nice cheese to sauce ratio. Sauce is slightly sweet and tangy. Good crust, it was a good pizza, just not $5.50/$4.50 worth in my opinion.

We wanted to try NYC style pizza and the reviews for Joe’s pizza were as outstanding. We reached the place and there we see a huge line to get the pizza by slice or whole pie.
We told ourselves that this is it. It shall be worth the wait.
It took about 30-40 minutes to get to order and get the pie.
It was okay not the best that we had. I didn’t understand how come it’s rated this high on Google.
Nothing bad about the pizza but nothing best either.
Just wanted to let people know if you are spending the 30-40 minutes in December cold to have this pie may be think about it. You shall get it when there is no line.
So the disappointment is less.

Food: 4 Stars
Service: 4 Stars
Ambience: 4 Stars
Value: 5 Stars
Sanitary: 4 Stars
Overall: 4.2 Stars

Note: CASH ONLY

Joe’s Pizza in NYC has been on my food bucket list for ages, and I finally made the stop. I still remember watching Worth It on BuzzFeed years ago when they crowned Joe’s as the “most worth it” pizza, so there was definitely some nostalgia walking through those doors.

I ordered the classic cheese slice — simple, timeless, and honestly the best way to judge a good pizzeria. It didn’t disappoint. The cheese was fresh and melty without being greasy, the sauce had that perfect tang, and the crust… chef’s kiss. It had just the right thickness with a crispy crunch that somehow still stayed soft inside. Exactly what you want from a New York slice.

In today’s economy, finding something tasty, reliable, and filling feels like a small win, and Joe’s definitely delivers on that comfort factor. It’s nothing overly fancy, but that’s the charm. It’s just solid, satisfying pizza that hits the spot.

Would I come back? Absolutely. It may not be life-changing, but it’s definitely a staple worth trying — especially if you grew up watching the same food videos that made Joe’s a must-visit in the first place.

xx kellychan360

The pizza at Joe’s Pizza was very good, and the slices are huge! It was exactly what we were looking for.

We didn’t realize it was cash-only, but thankfully there’s an ATM right outside the shop, which made it easy. There wasn’t a line when we stopped in on February 16th, so it was a quick and convenient visit.

We chose this spot over John’s because we wanted to grab individual slices rather than order a whole pie. It was the perfect choice for a fast, no-fuss stop. There isn’t much seating, but we weren’t expecting there to be.

We would definitely go again!

’ve been hunting for a REAL New York slice for weeks — not the overpriced tourist versions or the soggy cafeteria ones that taste like cardboard. Almost gave up…
until a local recommended Joe’s Pizza in Greenwich Village.

The moment I walked in, I knew something was different — the smell of real cheese, the thin crispy crust coming straight out of the oven, and slices cut confidently, not shyly.

I ordered a plain cheese slice — because if a place can’t nail the basics, nothing else matters.

First bite… and honestly?
THIS is the slice I’ve been looking for.
Crispy edge, airy crust, light tomato tang, and cheese that actually stretches — authentic, simple, perfect.

The staff worked fast even with a line out the door — and everyone inside looked like someone who knows pizza. No Instagram tourists — just locals and real NYC regulars.

⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ 5/5 — Worth every minute of the wait.
If you want to taste actual New York… not the fake version… start with a plain slice at Joe’s.
I stopped by Joe’s Pizza on one of those evenings when New York feels overwhelming — when the noise, the speed, and the rush make you forget to slow down.
And somehow… holding that simple slice in my hand brought me back to myself.

Crispy edge, warm cheese, thin New York crust — nothing fancy, just honest flavor.
It reminded me that sometimes the simplest things are the most comforting.

⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐
A perfect NY slice — authentic, warm, and unforgettable.

SENSATIONAL PIZZA 🥇🥇

Had a urge for 2 slices and just happened to see Joe’s Pizza up the block. Luckily there were 2 parking spots out front.

Ran over quickly and grabbed a regular slice & mushroom slice to go. Not much of a wait for the winter season. But there is usually a line by the door.

Pizza done just right. Thin crust with a flavorful tomato sauce and cheese still oozing a bit. 👍👍

Cash only!

A no-nonsense place to get a solid slice of pizza or a whole pie. I enjoyed the cheese and the mozzarella slices the most especially after adding some oregano and garlic powder.

I also noticed, If you give a tip the worker will often heat your slice before handing it over. This can be really clutch if you happen to get it by the slice, you can get unlucky with one of the last slices from what they have out.

The pizza was thin, firm, and very tasty. My experience was during lunch and it was very crowded. If you go plan on standing or waiting for a table. When your getting a pizza where Spiderman worked your gonna have crowds. Solid slice for the money!

Probably the most famous pizza joint in NYC — and for good reason! There are several Joe’s Pizza locations around the city, but the Carmine Street one is the original and has that classic, historic vibe.

I got a pepperoni slice and it was really good — fresh, hot, and full of flavor. It’s cash only, but there’s an ATM right at the front, so no problem there.

A must-visit for anyone who loves authentic New York pizza!

Joe’s Pizza was honestly underwhelming. The pizza itself was average at best and definitely not worth the hype. What made the experience worse was that they only accept cash, so I had to find an ATM and pay extra fees just to order. The place felt dirty, and watching the person at the counter drop slices directly on the counter was pretty off-putting. Overall, nothing about the experience justifies the high ratings—there are much better pizza spots in Manhattan.

It’s a pizza, essentially just flour and simple ingredients. I understand that many people enjoy pizza, but let’s be honest: the quality here doesn’t match the $5–6 price per slice.

The place itself was dirty, had no service, and only accepted cash.

Overall, not worth the cost.
Awesome pizza! Try and go at weird times or you might have to wait in line. Also, super limited seating, true New York slice of pizza though, and cheap!

We got a slice with pepperoni for 5.50 each (this seemed a little expensive…). The pizza slice was good and big but extremely greasy. Someone next to me even had to absorb the oil with a napkin before eating… But except that it was good. I went because it’s iconic but wouldn’t come again

It's a New York City staple, a slice of cheese pizza will light up your heart. Slices come out of the oven hot, and there's enough foot traffic to ensure it doesn't sit around. Joe's pizza is one of the best Top 10 for NYC pizza in my opinion. The dough is nice and fresh well done is a must...cheese and sauce as a whole phenomenal. The staff and servers are friendly and polite. Lines aren't too bad, and move quickly. The stream of tourists is a good indication of how popular this place is. There's a park across from it to sit and eat...100% recommend!

Excellent NYC pizza!   We got in pretty quickly. Cash only. And the ATM right by the entrance - $3.50 fee.    $5 slice of regular.
Better off buying.a whole pie.

Bought a few slices of pepperoni and combo. The pepperoni was a good sized slice covered in pepperoni. Add some pepper flakes and this tastes great for a late night bite. Pepperoni is their most popular and they get purchased as soon as they come out of the oven. The combo is a solid choice as well if you want a little more of everything on your pizza. The green peppers have a good crunch to them and it’s generously portioned with mushroom and olives too. Lines move pretty fast despite how long they can get even at late hours. The staff are no nonsense and quick to get you your slices and pies. The general atmosphere is busy with lots of decor proving how long they’ve been around from all the celebrity photos over the years. Generally not much in the way of seating, it’s mostly standing space which is fine inside and outside. Can get pretty hot outside so it’s nice they have a front window open to let some cool air in to offset the hot ovens.

If you want to try the classic NYC cheese slice this is a great place. Nothing fancy.. the sauce is good, the crust is ok, it is not as cruncy as other slices like Bleecker street. I personally prefer Bleecker street pizza, but this one is good too.

Super fast service, cool vibes, and grumpy (in a good way) servers who know what they’re doing. Solid pizza overall but it’s much MUCH better straight out of the oven (obviously) than after it’s been resting so definitely worth waiting a few minutes for a fresh batch
Cash only is a downside

The pizza was excellent—light, flavorful, and not greasy at all. It was served at a good temperature and counter crew was super friendly too . The dough was perfectly thin, with just the right texture. Overall, a great spot.

I thought that this pizza slice was good but not exceptional given all of the hype and praise it receives in the media. It is cash only as a heads up and the workers weren’t the most welcoming. I would have liked the slice just a bit crispier and less greasy. It is overall still a good slice worth trying but there are better options out there.

The pizza was excellent—light, flavorful, and not greasy at all. It was served at a good temperature (though I wouldn’t have minded it being a touch hotter). The dough was perfectly thin, with just the right texture, and you can really tell the difference that quality water makes. Overall, a great spot for a quick and satisfying fix—I’d definitely come back.”

Finally had a chance to see if the hype was real about this pizza and it was! Nice thin and crispy pizza perfect ratio of sauce to cheese to crust small spot grab a slice and go or a pie 4.50 a slice but quality and taste was worth it not greasy great slice great quick bite

Out of town family wanted to check JOE'S Pizza out. Nice and fresh just of course busy due all the customers.  Thankfully the weather was still nice we could eat outside.
The area was really cool and historic in some parts.

CASH ONLY! UGHHHH. Anyway, went to Joe’s (after dinner lol) and was great. Don’t expect crazy service, it is what it is. I wish they would warm the slices but understand they don’t to control the flow of people. Old school for sure and worth the visit, even if cash only…but come on, at least introduce Apple Pay!

Don't go there for the atmosphere. Good to tick off the tourist list. The pizza is nice. Situated in heart of a food lover's heaven in NY. Go for a walk to other places in the area. Yes this pizza place needs a bouncer !!

Speedy, excellent slice and similar price to all ‘hot spots’.
Famous for a reason, lots of people will always say it’s not the best, but it’s always gonna be a top 10 for consistency across branches over the years!
This was our first time visiting here.  Friendly staff & great customer service.  The pizza was amazing & delicious.  Definitely, will travel back for the pizza. CASH ONLY place!

We tried Joe’s Pizza for the first time and ordered a full pizza—it was huge! We went with the spinach on a tomato base, and it was fantastic. Fresh ingredients, great flavor, and that classic New York thin crust made it a perfect first experience. You have to wait a bit in the queue but The vibe is great.
Delicious, classic Manhattan staple. Open late, hot and fresh pizza. Huge NY slices. Super loud and crowded. Worth it every time. We love Joe’s.
Amazing pizza! If you can, visit this spot instead of the times square one. There is much smaller queue :)
Quintessential NYC pizza at its finest. Nothing fancy, nothing crazy, just walk in grab a slice or two and go. No two hours lines, no attitude just friendly people and a great slice.  #doyouknowrex

Was expecting a little seating, but stayed for the pizza 🍕
Super busy, super fast service, and now I get the hype. Just a simple cheese slice — soft inside, crispy crust, no overthinking. Limited options, but I guess that’s what keeps it quick and good.
Honestly, nothing special. It’s just the usual pizza. I’ve had better. But the service was good. Long lines but quick. The pizza was affordable as well for its size. 😊
First ever New York pizza for me (yeah I’m not living in the US). Crunchy / crispy dough and very soft and yummy toppings. Would definitely recommend going here. But keep in mind cash only

I am convinced that might be the best pizza I have ever had.  My son tells me it is exactly what he was hoping for and he was not disappointed.  The crust was amazing.  The cheese was fantastic.  The under-char was perfect.  The pizza oozes NYC.  I'm so glad I went.
You can only pay with cash, not by card, but there’s an ATM right in front of Joe’s Pizza to withdraw money. The pizzas were very, very good. I’ll definitely keep it in mind for my next trip

Absolutely the BEST cheese pizza in NYC!

Joe’s Pizza is a New York City legend for a reason. The cheese slice here is perfection—crispy, thin crust with just the right amount of chew, tangy tomato sauce, and perfectly melted mozzarella that stretches with every bite. It’s simple, classic, and absolutely addictive.

No frills, just authentic NYC street pizza done right. Whether you're a local or visiting the city for the first time, this is a must-stop. Grab a slice, stand at the counter, and experience what real New York pizza is all about.

Pro tip: don’t overthink it—just get the cheese slice. It’s what they’re famous for, and it never disappoints.
CASH Only! Great classic NY slice. It was a little char and crispy. I would come back.

Classic NY joint. Best one down in the Village on Carmine but if you're in midtown and you got the hankering,  the Times Square one will do,  but it's often jammed with tourists and had a long line unless it's crappy weather. Get the Sicilian. You won't be disappointed.

Their pizzas weren’t good at all considering all the fame and hype of the chain. It felt like the pizzas you’d find at a school cafeteria. The service and atmosphere were as to be expected for a pizza chain.
Great pizza. Worth queing if in a central location. Great value for money

Got a slice after drinks and there was a small line and nowhere really to eat. The vibe feels very classic new York. The pizza itself was pretty good but I'm giving 4 stars because they didn't warm it up and it tasted a little stale. The fresh cheese slice our friend had was much better. Great price though.
Joes was a great slice! We were there later and there was no line and a place to sit.

Awesome pizza for a good price. Nothing better than a slice of pizza in NYC. Love this spot. It's fast and the white pie is so good I could eat a whole pie. Thin perfect crust, perfect seasoning. Have to leave the city so I don't eat here 5 times a day.

Great no frills place in the heart of New York.

Famous for appearing in Spiderman 2, this pizza place serves up a bit of nostalgia for movie buffs.

They also have  a "wall of fame" of all the famous celebrities who have passed through the doors over the years including Oscar winner Adrien Brody.

Pizza slices are reasonably priced and massive! I didn't try it myself due to allergies however, my family thought it was one of the best margheritas they ever had 🤤
First time in NYC trying Joe's Pizza and we can say we get the hype! The spot is very small and crowded but other than that the service and food is pretty solid!
It’s decent. It’s not mind blowing or crazy unique, but it tastes pretty good, is iconic, and is easily accessible.

My friends and I went to Joe's Pizza and tried five different signature slices—each one was delicious! The crust was perfectly crispy, and the toppings were fresh. We had a great time, but the place was pretty crowded. Still, it’s definitely worth it for some of the best pizza in town!
A true example of what NY pizza is and should be. No frills , just a greatvwell made slice.

🍕 royalty.

Unrivalled and Undefeated.

MVP of the slice game.

Your favourite pizza place’s favourite pizza place.

I tried all three variations- they were okay if not bland. I was trying to find the flavor and hype especially after not eating all day, it was underwhelming. Nice staff and great New York vibe with some fast service but I wish there were more options and more seasoning in the sauce or something. Price is also pretty good for portion

Joe's Pizza in Manhattan is an absolute slice of heaven! The moment you sink your teeth into their pizza, you're transported to a world of exquisite flavors and authenticity. The crust? Perfection. Crispy yet chewy, it's the ideal foundation for the flavorful toppings that burst with freshness. The sauce-to-cheese ratio? Spot on. Each bite is a symphony of taste that resonates with anyone craving a true New York-style pizza experience. Joe's Pizza is an iconic establishment that sets the bar high for pizza aficionados everywhere.
While there might not be parking or ample seating, the hustle and bustle adds to its authenticity. It’s a testament to its popularity, where folks line up eagerly for a slice of that renowned pizza. It’s a small sacrifice for the big reward of savoring some of the best pizza the city has to offer.

I came in with high hopes, but left unsatisfied. I tried 3 slices: cheese, pepperoni, & mozzarella.

The positives:
•Service was quick & easy
•Pizza was moderately priced for its size

The negatives:
•Cash only (atm is available just outside for a $3.50 service fee - ouch)
•Tomato sauce on all 3 slices that we tried were very watery and lacked flavor
•Cheese slice lacked personality
•Pepperoni slice was slightly better but I had grease dripping onto my fingers and hand
•Mozzarella slice was not worth it - couldn’t even taste the [thin] pieces of mozzarella

Overall, I wouldn’t recommend.
Joe’s is definitely overhyped.

We loved Joe’s so much we came twice while in town. It was delicious and affordable. It’s not as cheap as some of the places but you pay for quality. For 4 slices of pizza and three drinks we spent $27. This location is cash only so beware of that. They do have an ATM out front. The staff was super friendly. Highly recommend coming here. Multiple locations throughout the city. I would skip the Times Square location due to the crowds.

We stumbled across this pizza place by accident and by the crowds around it, it seemed to be good! We had slices of cheese, pepperoni and mozzarella and all were delicious! Thin and crispy and cheesy. Cash only with a handy atm out the front. If you’re in the area highly recommend but be prepared to stand and eat outside.

This is your classic NY slice. It's famously where the original Spider-Man was filmed. Nothing too wild, but it's in a cool part of town. Definitely worth grabbing a slice; the Sicilian was particularly good. Was my wife’s favorite!

I had a slice of cheese pizza and it was good.  The crust has a doughier taste than other places that I've tried in Manhattan.  I can see how that might be off-putting for some people, but I liked the different flavor for a change of pace.  The sauce to cheese ratio is great.  It's not my most favorite, but I'd certainly eat it again.  Definitely worth trying if you're in the area.  Just don't go to the one by Times Square.  It's not worth the wait.  Go to one of the other locations.  Even then, expect crowds and plan to eat standing outside.
Best NY pizza? No. But, did I see this place in the Spider-man movie 20+ years ago so sometimes when I visit NYC, I pay too much cash for a mid slice of pepperoni? Yes, yes, I do.

The Spider-Man pizza — omg — it was so delicious I’d go back for it again and again. It instantly became my favorite! The slices were super hot, thin-crust, with just the right amount of pepperoni and flavorful cheese. The place is small and there’s not much seating, but it’s absolutely worth eating there. One thing to keep in mind: they only accept cash, no cards — so be prepared! I also noticed they don’t serve ketchup with the pizza like we usually do in Mexico, but adding some grated cheese is a nice touch if you want extra flavor. I totally recommend Joe’s Pizza — I really hope I can come back someday!

We were staying at the hotel just 2 minutes away and we didn't even know this was the pizza joint from the original spider man movie until we got closer in the queue to order. Really cool though! But regardless, it is simply and so absolutely bizarre the diehard fanatics of this one particular joe's pizza out of the many other similar pizza shops there are in NYC. We only queued up because of the sheer size of the queue and to be honest, it probably wasn't worth the wait. It felt more like an event to queue up and order a pizza from the famous spider-man pizza shop than anything. The staff were super friendly and chatty, and the pizza was pretty good, but it was certainly not worth the 30 minute line up. To everyone who spent half an hour here just for a slice of pizza too, you're insane!

This used to be the prototype in some ways. And I won't lie; this was my first NYC slice because locals said so when I was first visiting in 2003. It style produces a decent slice but all charm is gone. Not unlike the cutt to be honest. But no matter what, I have a soft spot for this location. And more specifically, the slices.

Still the best.  Used to live nearby and we come back here anytime we come to NYC.

Crust is perfect, just the right amount of crisp and firmness. Slice isn’t too thick so not too filling.  Cheese and sauce are delicious and sauce has good tangy flavour.

Fast service and slices always hot and ready to go because they do so much business.

Authentic NYC style pizza. Their pizza is so yummy! The absolute best in NYC. Always fresh b/c sells out as soon as it comes out of the oven. Slices are much larger than the midtown location, and there is no long line like midtown. Thin crust, crispy but also chewy. Great sauce and not too salty or hard. Super delicious. Would recommend. Sorry we were so hungry and ate it as soon as it came out of the oven. Therefore didn't think to take photo! Will do next time and add. Three pizza choices: cheese, margarita, pepperoni.

This is our second visit to Joe’s Pizza. We first tried it in fall 2023, and back then it was great. This time, we had the same pepperoni pizza, but honestly, we don’t think it was worth the long wait. I understand the hype partly comes from its appearance in the Spider-Man movie, but does it really matter if you only see the pizzeria for a few minutes on screen?!

Great place to get a slice. Kind of iconic for NYC pizza. While I preferred John's down the street, this was very good. I liked how they sold pizza by the slice (John's doesn't do that) but it was inconvenient to have to pay with cash. There is an ATM right next to the entrance but I hate ATM fees. Would recommend though especially if you're hunting for the best NYC pizza.
Ive been wanting this ever since spider-man 2 came out and at long last i was able to say “pizza time”

Tried Joe’s Pizza (vegan/vegetarian option), and while it was quite basic, it definitely gives you that classic New York slice experience. Nothing fancy, but a must-try at least once when you’re in the city!

Not worth the hype. We were on vacation from Wisconsin, and came here based on a YouTube recommendation. We were thoroughly disappointed.

I prefer our Midwestern Chicago deep dish pizzas any day :)

Joe's Pizza was bland and people here were rude. The lines were long (I am sure because of the hype), and when we reached the counter, realized that it's cash only??! What?! Why?! It's so popular, and still they don't want to go digital?! There is an ATM outside of the store. Side business maybe? Shady enough for me.

Coming back to the food, the slice was paper-thin and and surely not worth the price of USD 4.50 for a cheese.

We used up all our cash here and still were hungry as before; hungry enough to go next door to Adobo and enjoy a hearty fulfilling and satisfying meal to end our day in New York.

A classic New York slice done right. Joe’s Pizza is super fast—walk in, grab your slice, and you’re out. It’s cash-only, but the quality makes it worth the stop. They don’t waste a second and still manage to deliver consistently great, high-quality pizza to every customer.
The pizza was excellent! Somehow it manages to be thin and crispy, but still soft at the same time. Really tasty and satisfying.
I went on a Tuesday around 8:30pm. No lines and delicious pizza!
Shame on you Joe. Get it together!! 💔 Recently, I had pizza from one of your trucks out in LA that was better than this slice. I don’t care if it’s 1:40 in the morning, that’s your whole thing.

What a gem! I looked up the best pizza in NYC, just hoping for a good slice of pie — but this was way better than I expected! I folded the slice, and the mozzarella cheese grease oozed out… pure perfection. Let me tell you — AMAZING! So happy I stumbled upon Joe’s. Can’t wait to come back for another slice of heaven!

They operate fast for how many people there can be at times. I think it’s definitely living off some Spider-Man hype and fame, it’s a tourist spot. The slices are great New York slices but there are better in the city. Sicilian was alright.

I am so disappointed! Joe’s used to be the best place like 10 years ago and ever since the slices have gotten smaller with less cheese and tomato sauce. Today I ordered a regular slice and there was barely any cheese. The slice was tiny and there was almost no tomato sauce. The crust was also thin, but not a thin crust way - in an anemic New York pizza way. The crust was also burned, but I’m assuming that that might just be a one off. I’m giving food 2 stars because it’s actually worse than just OK. I hope they listen to reviews and up their game. It would be sad to lose such a great New York institution.

Joe’s Pizza in New York is an iconic spot with a slice that truly lives up to the hype. The thin crust and perfectly balanced sauce make it a must-visit for any pizza lover. Fans of Spider-Man will also appreciate the nostalgic vibe, as the place famously featured in the movies. Whether you’re a local or a tourist, Joe’s serves up a classic New York slice that’s hard to beat. Don’t miss it when you’re in the city!
Small place...pizza was a little too dark on the bottom for my liking...ordered two slices of cheese pizza which were very large in size, but okay...

After a long day of walking, we enjoyed having Joe’s Pizza for dinner! Slices are quite big and $4 dlls each, take into account they only accept cash tho, there’s an ATM right outside. Place is busy but goes and comes, there’s also all types of spices and sauces you can add in the tables.

I have no idea why anyone thinks this place is special. It's the same quality as any other slice shop but smaller and with longer lines. There are a thousand places in NYC to get a similar slice. Its fine, nothing wrong with it, but its just average.

Unpleasant. I recently visited Joe's Pizza, and unfortunately, it did not live up to the hype. Bedford's rule. The place was quite dirty, and the staff seemed indifferent, which made the overall experience unpleasant. It felt like they were relying on their reputation rather than delivering quality service or food. The pizza itself was underwhelming, lacking the flavor and quality I expected. It's clear that they’re popular, but I was left with the impression that they don’t really care about the customer experience anymore. I wouldn't recommend going out of your way to eat here.

New york style pizza that was mentioned in the Toby Maguire Spiderman. Located near one of the metro, serving pizza, quick and easy.
There are some tall tables outside the restaurant. The food came very fast, just hand the money and they hand you the food.
Worth the wait and exactly what you want when someone ask to taste NY pizza.

A true NYC legend—and it deserves the title. Perfect flavor, crisp crust, and exactly what you want from a New York slice. The staff at the West Village location were especially kind and welcoming, chido carnales. Just note it’s cash only, and depending on the time it can get crowded—but absolutely worth it.

Known from spiderman, is Joe's pizza. I think it hasn't had the same owner for a long time and it's a bit of an unattractive place to look at. But friendly staff and the pizza was very tasty. We took the large pizza pepperoni and had just enough to eat with 2 adults and 2 children. You can only sit inside with 2 people so take pizza with you and eat it in the nearby park (recommended) Note that you can only pay with cash.
Amazing cheese slice. It was a melt in your mouth slice of pizza! Must hit pizza spot if folks visit NYC! At $4 for a cheese slice it's just incredible value.

Our reviews had over 52 million views last year.  We do not get paid we just love to eat and have fun.  We really loved Joe's.  We are very picky when it comes to pizza but this is top 3 in NYC for sure.  Very small place with no tables, but 4 stools you can use if you must.  We prefer to go across the street to the park to eat like most people do who come here.  Very short menu.  Just a few slices (round or square) and just a few flavors.  I tried almost all of them and they were all awesome.  I love square, she loves round.  Both were super good.  She liked the plain cheese pie best, I liked the pepperoni.  THIS IS THE BEST PIZZA IN NYC FOR SURE.  WE ARE NYC BROOKLYN NATIVES.  Check out all of our reviews. If we do not like it we do no review it so all of the ones you see are places that are fantastic. Standing beneath the 1,083-foot iron lattice of the Eiffel Tower is a surreal experience that feels like stepping directly into a postcard of Parisian history. The atmosphere on the first floor has improved greatly with the addition of the transparent glass floor, which provides a dizzying view of the crowds below and makes for a fantastic thrill. The only major drawback remains the aggressive street vendors and the persistent crowds near the base, which can detract from the romantic ambiance. However, if you time your visit for sunset, you get to witness the transition from the golden hour to the spectacular hourly light sparkle, which remains one of the most magical sights in the world. It is a logistically demanding visit that requires booking months in advance on TripAdvisor or the official site, but the payoff is a profound sense of place that defines the entire Paris experience.

Eiffel Tower, a wrought - iron structure located in Paris is a technological masterpiece in building histories.
It was designed and built during 1887 by Gustave Eiffel and then was named in his honor too.

Having a height of 1,083 feet, a  weight of 10,000 tons and revited by 2.5 million rivets, this wondrous scape became the entrance gateway to the International exposition in 1889.
It was erected in two years, with a small labor force and at a low cost.  Designed as a well lit, airy, strong structure, which pioneered a revolution in civil engineering.

It remarkably stands on four lattice girder piers. The glass cage machines were designed by the US Otis Elevator Company, which later became the main feature of the building.

Though, Modifications were made for further international expositions of 1900, 1925, and 1937 but Additions to the tower were made for television transmissions only wherein 66 feet were added to it's height.

The tower features a museum (which we were unable to see), restaurants, and a much talked about Eiffel’s Reception Room providing space for business conferences, cultural events, and social gatherings.
An observation deck is located just under the antenna, at 906 feet.

Going up the tower is absolutely worth it. The views over Paris are stunning, especially on a clear day. You get a full sense of how beautiful and elegant the city is, with the Seine winding through it and landmarks visible in every direction. Even just spending time at the base, walking around and taking photos, feels special.

Yes, it can get crowded, and lines can be long if you don’t plan ahead. Buying tickets in advance definitely helps. Security is well organized, and staff do their best to keep things moving smoothly despite the number of visitors.

At night, the experience becomes even more magical. When the tower lights up and sparkles, it creates one of the most memorable moments you can have in Paris. It’s romantic, iconic, and something you’ll remember long after your trip is over. A true must-see.

An iconic landmark that still manages to exceed expectations. Up close, the iron structure feels surprisingly elegant, and each level reveals a wider, more beautiful view of Paris. The highlight is returning at night when the tower sparkles and the whole city feels magical. A must-visit that truly lives up to its reputation.

The store is considered one of several Apple flagship locations, and the pre-eminent store for Apple in New York City. The store is on and beneath a public plaza by the General Motors Building, built in 1968. Its exposed exterior is a transparent 32 ft (9.8 m) cube in the middle of the plaza. The plaza is partly lined with benches and trees. The substantive interior, below ground, features a reflective steel spiral staircase and elevator, wooden tables with Apple products, and rooms and areas for specific Apple products.

Visiting the Empire State Building’s observation deck is nothing short of magical — the kind of experience that reminds you why New York City is called the city that never sleeps and why people from all over the world fall in love with it again and again.

From the moment you step inside, you’re wrapped in the building’s rich Art Deco elegance. The exhibits whisk you through history, giving you a sense of the ambition and brilliance that brought this iconic skyscraper to life. By the time you reach the elevators, you already feel like you’re part of something timeless.

But then — the doors open, and there it is: a panorama so breathtaking it feels like the city is unfolding just for you.

The observation deck is a place where skyscrapers look small, taxis move like fireflies, and the Hudson gleams like a ribbon of light. Whether you visit by day, when every building stands crisp and proud, or at night, when the city sparkles like a sea of stars, the view is pure enchantment. It's the kind of sight that quiets the world for a moment and fills you with awe.

What makes it even lovelier is the atmosphere — peaceful, breezy, and surprisingly intimate. Couples whisper dreams into the wind, friends share gasps of wonder, and families point out landmarks with the excitement of discovering New York for the first time.

It’s more than an observation deck. It’s a reminder of how high human imagination can climb — and how beautiful the world can look from just a little closer to the clouds.

A truly unforgettable experience, perfect for dreamers, romantics, and anyone who wants to feel the heartbeat of New York from above.

• Ticketed entry & observation decks: Entry to the Empire State Building’s observatories is ticketed — standard access includes the 86th-floor Main Deck, and a combined 86th + 102nd-floor Top Deck ticket is available. Book timed tickets online to avoid lines.

• Hours & seasonality: The observatory operates year-round (open most days) with evening hours for city-lights views; check the official hours the day of your visit because special events or maintenance can change opening times.

• Ticket types & express options: Besides standard tickets, the ESB sells Express Pass options (86th or 86th+102nd) that expedite entry — useful at peak times but more expensive. Prices vary by time/date and dynamic pricing can push peak fares higher.

• What you’ll see & why go: The 86th deck offers wide 360° views (Manhattan grid, Central Park, Hudson & East Rivers); the renovated 102nd floor adds floor-to-ceiling panoramic windows and a premium experience with longer sightlines on clear days. Allow 45–90 minutes.

• Best times for photos & fewer crowds: Midday (about 12–2pm) often sees lighter lines after the morning rush; sunrise and sunset offer spectacular light but draw the most visitors and higher-priced slots — plan accordingly.

• Access & transit: The building is on 34th St between Fifth and Sixth Avenues — walkable from Penn Station (MTA) and Herald Square subways; cabs and rideshares drop near the curb. Use the official directions page for the most efficient route.

• Security & bag policy: Strict bag rules apply — large backpacks and suitcases are generally not permitted; only small clutches/clear bags within specified dimensions are allowed (medical/diaper bags subject to search). There is no on-site bag check.

• Accessibility: The attraction is ADA-accessible with elevators and accessible restrooms; check the ESB accessibility page or call guest services for specific mobility needs.

• Costs & planning note: Base prices start (officially) from the 86th-floor fare and rise for the 102nd or express options — booking online is strongly recommended and remember extra booking fees may apply. Expect higher rates at sunset or peak demand.

• What to keep in mind

Timed tickets & queues: Even with a timed ticket you pass security — express passes reduce waiting but are pricier.

Weather & visibility: Views depend on weather — clear days give the farthest visibility (up to many miles); fog/rain limit sightlines.

Sunrise/sunset tradeoffs: Sunrise gives quiet photos but requires very early entry packages; sunset is dramatic but crowded and may have surge pricing.

No large bags / limited facilities: Travel light — bag rules and security checks are enforced and there’s limited storage.

The Statue of Liberty was officially welcomed to New York’s harbor on October 26, 1886, marking a celebration of liberty and democracy, and serving as a symbolic gift from France to the United States. Over the 135 years since Lady Liberty’s arrival, the nation has evolved significantly, yet the core symbolism she embodies remains steadfast. The statue’s full name is Liberty Enlightening the World, reflecting its purpose to serve as a beacon of freedom. It was gifted by France to America in 1886 as a gesture of friendship and shared ideals. The figure depicts Libertas, the Roman goddess of freedom, clothed in a flowing robe. The statue stands approximately 93 meters (305 feet) tall from base to torch and weighs about 204 metric tonnes (around 450,000 pounds). Visitors must ascend a staircase of 354 steps within the pedestal to reach the statue’s crown. The crown features 25 windows, symbolizing enlightenment and hope. Its seven spikes represent the seven continents and seven oceans, emphasizing the universal nature of liberty and human rights. Additionally, the likeness of the statue’s face is believed to be modeled after the sculptor Frédéric Auguste Bartholdi’s mother, Charlotte, capturing a gentle and determined expression. Please use the Authorised Ferry service, State City Cruises, which takes you to the Statue of Liberty Island and Ellis Island.

The Statue of Liberty, officially titled Liberty Enlightening the World, is perhaps the most recognizable symbol of freedom in the world. Standing on Liberty Island in New York Harbor, it was a gift from the people of France to the United States to celebrate the centennial of the Declaration of Independence and the enduring friendship between the two nations.

The Visionaries: The idea was proposed in 1865 by French political thinker Édouard de Laboulaye. It was designed by sculptor Frédéric Auguste Bartholdi, while the internal iron framework was engineered by Gustave Eiffel (who later built the Eiffel Tower).

A Transatlantic Effort: France funded the statue itself, while the United States was responsible for the pedestal. When American fundraising stalled, newspaper publisher Joseph Pulitzer launched a successful crowdfunding campaign that gathered small donations from over 120,000 people.

Assembly: Built in Paris and completed in 1884, the statue was disassembled into 350 pieces, packed into 214 crates, and shipped across the Atlantic. It was finally dedicated on October 28, 1886.

The Torch: Representing enlightenment, the current torch is a 1986 replacement covered in 24k gold leaf (the original is now in the museum).

The Tablet: Held in her left hand, it is inscribed with "JULY IV MDCCLXXVI" (July 4, 1776), the date of American independence.

The Crown: Its seven spikes represent the seven continents and seven seas, signaling that the message of liberty is universal.

Broken Shackles: Often missed by visitors because they are at her feet, the broken chains and shackles symbolize the end of slavery and oppression.
